title: High-temperature superconductivity: forty years of an open problem
description: A companion to our short video: what makes the copper oxides special, what experiments have settled, and why the pairing mechanism is still debated.

video.caption: From zero resistance and BCS theory, through the cuprates, d-wave pairing, the pseudogap and the strange metal, to the Hubbard model, iron pnictides, hydrides and nickelates.

sections.heading: From zero resistance to Cooper pairs
paragraphs: In 1911, Kamerlingh Onnes found that mercury lost all measurable electrical resistance below about four kelvin. Two decades later, Meissner and Ochsenfeld showed that a superconductor also expels magnetic fields. Zero resistance and the Meissner effect together define the superconducting state.

Bardeen, Cooper and Schrieffer explained conventional superconductors in 1957. Lattice vibrations, or phonons, produce an effective attraction that binds electrons into Cooper pairs, and the pairs condense into a single coherent state. Estimates based on phonon pairing suggested that transition temperatures would stay near a few tens of kelvin. This was an empirical expectation, not a strict bound.

sections.heading: The copper-oxide surprise
paragraphs: In 1986, Bednorz and Müller reported superconductivity in a lanthanum–barium–copper oxide at around 35 kelvin. Within a year, Wu, Chu and coauthors found superconductivity at 93 kelvin in a Y–Ba–Cu–O compound, later identified as YBa₂Cu₃O₇, above the 77 kelvin boiling point of liquid nitrogen. Cooling suddenly became cheap, and the field exploded.

Every cuprate shares one structural motif: the copper-oxygen plane. In the undoped parent compound, each copper carries a single hole in the d_{x²−y²} orbital. Band theory then predicts a half-filled band and hence a metal. Instead, strong on-site repulsion localizes the electrons, and the parent compound is a Mott insulator with antiferromagnetic order.

Removing electrons, which is called hole doping, destroys the antiferromagnet, and a superconducting dome rises in the temperature–doping phase diagram. Around it sit other puzzling regions: a pseudogap at lower doping, a strange metal above optimal doping, and a more conventional Fermi liquid on the heavily overdoped side.

sections.heading: What experiments have settled
paragraphs: The pairs in the cuprates are d-wave: the superconducting gap changes sign under a ninety-degree rotation. Phase-sensitive experiments made this decisive. In tricrystal rings designed so that a sign-changing gap forces frustration, Tsuei, Kirtley and coauthors observed half a flux quantum trapped spontaneously.

Angle-resolved photoemission maps the gap around the Fermi surface. It is largest near the antinodes, along the copper-oxygen bond directions, and vanishes along the diagonals, as the d-wave form requires. Above the transition temperature in underdoped samples, a pseudogap survives and leaves only disconnected Fermi arcs. Whether it reflects preformed pairs, a competing order, or both remains debated.

Near optimal doping, the resistivity is linear in temperature over a wide range, and in several materials the scattering rate approaches the so-called Planckian scale set by k_B T/ħ. Experiments also find charge and spin stripes, charge density waves and electronic nematicity. These orders appear intertwined with superconductivity rather than simply competing with it.

sections.heading: Models and the search for the glue
paragraphs: The minimal model is the Hubbard model: electrons hop between neighbouring sites with amplitude t and pay an energy U when two occupy the same site. In 1987, Anderson proposed that the Mott insulator hosts a resonating valence bond liquid of mobile singlets, which would become Cooper pairs on doping. The idea shaped decades of theory, though it remains unconfirmed.

Even this simple model is hard. Combining DMRG, quantum Monte Carlo, tensor networks and other methods, a multi-method study found stripe order in the underdoped ground state, nearly degenerate with d-wave superconducting states. Later work found that the pure Hubbard model with only nearest-neighbour hopping does not superconduct in the regime studied, while adding next-nearest-neighbour hopping can tip the balance. For those of us who develop tensor-network methods, this model is a demanding benchmark.

A leading candidate for the pairing glue is antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations. The interaction they mediate is repulsive and peaked at the antiferromagnetic wave vector Q. A repulsive interaction can still produce pairing if the gap has opposite signs at momenta connected by Q, which the d-wave form provides. This picture is widely used but not universally accepted.

sections.heading: New families, applications, and the open problem
paragraphs: In 2008, iron pnictides joined the family. They involve several orbitals and several Fermi pockets, and a widely discussed proposal is an s± gap that changes sign between electron and hole pockets. Under pressures above a million atmospheres, hydrides reached about 203 kelvin in H₃S and about 250 kelvin in LaH₁₀, with pairing that appears to be conventional and phonon mediated. Claims of room-temperature superconductivity near ambient conditions have not survived scrutiny.

Nickelates, chemical siblings of the cuprates, were found to superconduct in infinite-layer thin films in 2019. In 2023, signatures of superconductivity near 80 kelvin were reported in bilayer La₃Ni₂O₇ under pressure. Each new family tests which ingredients of cuprate physics are essential.

Meanwhile, the materials are already useful. REBCO coated-conductor tapes wind record magnets; a dc field of 45.5 tesla was reached with a high-temperature superconducting insert. They are used or being developed for NMR and MRI magnets, power cables, and compact fusion devices. Forty years on, however, the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity remains one of the great open problems in physics.

zh.title: 高温超导：一个悬而未决四十年的难题
zh.description: 配合我们短片的一篇文章：铜氧化物有何特别之处，实验已经确定了什么，以及配对机理为何至今仍有争论。
zh.videoCaption: 从零电阻与 BCS 理论出发，经由铜氧化物、d 波配对、赝能隙与奇异金属，一路讲到哈伯德模型、铁基超导、氢化物与镍氧化物。

sections.heading: 从零电阻到库珀对
paragraphs: 1911 年，昂内斯发现汞在大约四开尔文以下失去了一切可测的电阻。二十多年后，迈斯纳与奥克森菲尔德发现超导体还会排斥磁场。零电阻与迈斯纳效应共同定义了超导态。
1957 年，巴丁、库珀与施里弗解释了常规超导体。晶格振动（即声子）产生一种有效吸引，把电子束缚成库珀对，这些电子对凝聚为同一个相干态。基于声子配对的估计认为，转变温度会停留在几十开尔文附近。这是一种经验上的预期，而不是严格的上限。

sections.heading: 铜氧化物带来的意外
paragraphs: 1986 年，贝德诺尔茨与缪勒报告了一种镧钡铜氧化物在约 35 开尔文的超导。不到一年，吴茂昆、朱经武等人在一种 Y–Ba–Cu–O 化合物（后来确认为 YBa₂Cu₃O₇）中发现了 93 开尔文的超导，超过了液氮 77 开尔文的沸点。制冷一下子变得便宜，这个领域随之迅速发展。
所有铜氧化物都有一个共同的结构单元：铜氧平面。在未掺杂的母体化合物中，每个铜在 d_{x²−y²} 轨道上有一个空穴。能带理论据此预言一个半满能带，也就是金属。然而强烈的在位排斥使电子局域化，母体成为具有反铁磁序的莫特绝缘体。
移走电子，即所谓空穴掺杂，会破坏反铁磁序，一个超导“穹顶”在温度—掺杂相图中升起。它周围还有其他令人困惑的区域：低掺杂一侧的赝能隙、最佳掺杂之上的奇异金属，以及重度过掺杂一侧较为常规的费米液体。

sections.heading: 实验已经确定了什么
paragraphs: 铜氧化物中的电子对是 d 波的：超导能隙在转动九十度后改变符号。相位敏感实验使这一结论成为定论。在专门设计的三晶环中，变号的能隙会造成阻挫；Tsuei、Kirtley 等人在其中观测到了自发捕获的半个磁通量子。
角分辨光电子能谱绘出了费米面上的能隙。它在沿铜氧键方向的反节点附近最大，沿对角线方向消失，正符合 d 波形式的要求。在欠掺杂样品的转变温度之上，赝能隙依然存在，只留下彼此不相连的费米弧。它反映的是预先形成的电子对、一种竞争序，还是两者兼有，至今仍有争论。
在最佳掺杂附近，电阻率在很宽的温度范围内随温度线性变化；在若干材料中，散射率接近由 k_B T/ħ 给出的所谓普朗克尺度。实验还发现了电荷与自旋条纹、电荷密度波以及电子向列序。这些序与超导交织在一起，而不只是简单地相互竞争。

sections.heading: 模型，以及寻找“胶水”
paragraphs: 最简模型是哈伯德模型：电子以振幅 t 在相邻格点之间跃迁，两个电子占据同一格点时要付出能量 U。1987 年，安德森提出莫特绝缘体中存在由可移动单态构成的共振价键液体，掺杂后这些单态就会变成库珀对。这一想法影响了几十年的理论研究，但至今仍未得到证实。
即便是这个简单的模型也很难求解。一项结合 DMRG、量子蒙特卡罗、张量网络等多种方法的研究发现，欠掺杂区域的基态具有条纹序，并与 d 波超导态几乎简并。后来的工作发现，只含最近邻跃迁的纯哈伯德模型在所研究的参数区不超导，而加入次近邻跃迁可以改变这一平衡。对我们这些发展张量网络方法的人来说，这个模型是一个要求很高的基准。
配对“胶水”的一个主要候选者是反铁磁自旋涨落。它所传递的相互作用是排斥的，并在反铁磁波矢 Q 处达到峰值。只要能隙在由 Q 相连的动量上符号相反，排斥相互作用仍然可以导致配对，而 d 波形式恰好满足这一点。这一图像被广泛采用，但并未得到普遍接受。

sections.heading: 新的材料家族、应用与悬而未决的问题
paragraphs: 2008 年，铁基超导体加入了这个家族。它们涉及多个轨道和多个费米口袋，一个被广泛讨论的方案是在电子口袋和空穴口袋之间变号的 s± 能隙。在超过百万大气压的压强下，氢化物的超导温度达到约 203 开尔文（H₃S）和约 250 开尔文（LaH₁₀），其配对看来是常规的声子机制。接近常压条件的室温超导说法，至今都未能经受住检验。
镍氧化物是铜氧化物在化学上的“兄弟”。2019 年，人们在无限层薄膜中发现了它的超导。2023 年，有研究报告加压下的双层 La₃Ni₂O₇ 在接近 80 开尔文时出现超导迹象。每一个新家族都在检验铜氧化物物理中的哪些要素才是关键。
与此同时，这些材料已经派上用场。REBCO 涂层导体带材绕出了创纪录的磁体，借助高温超导插入线圈，人们实现了 45.5 特斯拉的直流磁场。它们已被用于或正被开发用于核磁共振谱仪与核磁共振成像的磁体、输电电缆以及紧凑型聚变装置。然而四十年过去，高温超导的机理仍是物理学中悬而未决的重大难题之一。
